title: Migration safety net, telemetry gates, and client guidance for API sunsetting
creator: Maya Chen
description: Purpose: Define a minimal, product-and-engineering-aligned runbook that ensures safe, observable, and reversible deprecation for the old transport and endpoint surface used by a subset of customers. This ticket captures the migration safety net (server-side adapters and canary fallbacks), the telemetry gating required to declare readiness at each phase, and the client-facing guidance and SDK adapters required to minimize customer disruption. The goal is to retire the stream-v0 and poll-v1 endpoints for hosted API consumers while preserving enterprise Dedicated/Private compatibility through a longer TTL and opt-in migration window.
background: stream-v0 and poll-v1 were implemented before unified transport; they still account for ~7% of hosted API calls during peak hours and are concentrated among older SDK versions.
Past deprecations (see PM-33122 and PM-26347) highlight gaps in telemetry gating and insufficient server-side compatibility adapters which increased customer support load.
We need a more conservative, telemetry-driven approach with explicit safety gates and server-side compatibility adapters so we can move faster in the future without causing outages.
scope_changes: IN: Build a server-side compatibility adapter (adapter-mode) that translates stream-v0/poll-v1 payloads to unified-infer requests for hosted API only.
IN: Add telemetry events and dashboards for migration health signals (error-rate-by-client-version, median-latency-change, fallback-rate).
IN: Publish SDK migration helpers (auto-upgrade flag and deprecation warning hooks) for JS, Python, and Go SDKs.
OUT: No forced changes to Dedicated control plane or Private air-gapped packages in this phase (those are handled by a separate enterprise migration plan).
acceptance_criteria: Server-side adapter is deployed behind a feature flag and can be enabled per-region without customer opt-in.

Telemetry dashboard is live with realtime metrics and historical comparison for the last 90 days: client-version distribution, conversion success rate, adapter-induced latency (p50/p90/p99), downstream model errors.
Migration safety gates defined and automated: gate_1 (conversion success >= 99% over 24h), gate_2 (error-rate delta <= 0.2%), gate_3 (no increase in incidents from impacted customers over 7 days).
SDKs (JS/Python/Go) publish migration helpers and a deprecation banner that appears at runtime for affected clients; at least 3 major customers validate the upgrade path in a pilot.
Runbook and rollback playbook published with step-by-step instructions and tested in a dry-run (see attachments for playbook artifact links).
Customer communication templates (email, Console banner, docs) drafted and approved by comms and legal.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Pilot, 2 weeks): Enable adapter-mode for a single low-risk region; invite 3 pilot customers; verify adapter conversion accuracy and latency impact.
Phase 1 (Gradual enable, 4 weeks): Ramp adapter to all hosted regions behind feature flags; monitor telemetry gates and perform weekly reviews with SRE and support.
Phase 2 (Announced migration window, 8 weeks): Notify remaining customers with migration checklist; SDK auto-upgrade helpers recommended; targeted outreach for top 10 customers using old endpoints.

Phase 3 (Hard deprecation for hosted, 2 weeks notice): If telemetry gates are green for 30 days, schedule final shutdown of stream-v0/poll-v1 for hosted API with 14-day notice; maintain adapter in passive logging mode for 90 days post-shutdown for diagnostics.
Enterprise (Dedicated/Private): Offer extended TTL and assisted migration (project-based) with security review; no hard shutdown until customer-signed completion.
telemetry_requirements: New events: migration.adapter.invocation, migration.adapter.success, migration.adapter.failure, client.old_endpoint.call, client.auto_upgrade.attempt
Dimensions: client_version, sdk_language, region, model_alias, customer_tier, request_size, sequence_length
Dashboards: Live view with p50/p90/p99 latency, adapter conversion latency, error-rate delta vs baseline, fallback-rate to unified transport
Alerts: Pager duty triggered if conversion success < 98% for >1h or adapter-induced p99 latency increases by >150ms vs baseline.
migration_checklist: Create adapter service and integration tests that assert parity of outputs for a curated prompt suite (see attachments).
Instrument adapter and runtime with the telemetry events and validate dashboard ingestion in staging; run mock load tests to measure latency delta.
Add feature flagging controls in Console to enable/disable adapter per-region and per-customer.
Prepare SDK migration helpers: (1) runtime warning banner, (2) auto-upgrade opt-in that rewrites transport calls, (3) telemetry hook for customers to opt into debug logs.
Legal/comms: Prepare terms update and customer-facing timeline; route PR to legal for review.
Support: Create troubleshooting KB and runbook for first-response and escalation to SRE/SE teams.
risks: Adapter introduces latency/regression for tail latency—could violate SLOs for some customers.
Incomplete telemetry could yield false-positive gate passes and lead to a problematic shutdown decision.
Large enterprise customers on Private/Dedicated may resist migration; dual-support increases operational complexity.
SDK auto-upgrade could inadvertently break edge-case client behaviors; need careful opt-in and telemetry.
mitigations: Keep adapter behind a per-region feature flag and throttle conversion for unknown client versions.
Require telemetry ingestion verification and a 72-hour observability freeze before moving phases forward.
Provide a paid migration assistance offering for Dedicated/Private customers and extend TTL if necessary.
Constrain SDK auto-upgrade to an opt-in flag by default; provide a dry-run mode that reports potential incompatibilities.
